subject.lede: Part page of the 100x plugin overview (explain/100x-plugin). Think of a writer who reads the draft once more before sending it, on purpose looking for the mistake they assume is there. When Claude finishes a turn that changed files or gave a long answer, a Stop hook holds the turn once and hands Claude a short prompt: assume this answer still has a mistake, name the three likeliest, check each against the files, fix or cut, then answer with one Re-check line. In blind runs that one extra pass is what caught a silent money bug no first answer caught. The hook never holds the same stop twice, and on any error it gets out of the way.

tldr.what: After a turn that edited files or gave a long answer, Claude is made to look again once, assuming it made a mistake, before the turn ends.
tldr.how: A Stop hook reads the end of the transcript, decides whether the turn was substantive and not yet re-checked, and blocks once with the prompt file's text as the reason.
tldr.watch_out: It is the same model checking itself, so it only helps when it actually opens the files; and manual mode still re-checks the engineer subagents.

context.purpose: When Claude has just edited code or written a long answer, you get a second, skeptical look at it without having to ask for one, and short questions stay fast.
context.why_now: Blind A/B runs found that the second pass, not its wording, is what turns a confident wrong answer into a right one; making it automatic means nobody has to remember it.

The measurements behind it, and every function in the hook, in the Code reference

entry_points.label: /100x:recheck typed by you

terms.means: A second, skeptical pass over the answer Claude just gave: assume a mistake, name the likeliest ones, check each against the files, fix what is real, cut what is not needed.
A script Claude Code runs when the main session tries to end its turn. It may block the stop once, with a reason Claude must act on.
The same moment for a subagent, a helper agent working on one task, when it finishes.
A turn that edited a file, with an edit tool or a shell command that writes one, or that ended in an answer at least {{min_chars}} long.
auto, the default, holds substantive turns; manual leaves the main session alone; off turns it off everywhere, subagents included.
Which subagent types are re-checked: off, all, or a list. Unset, it is the backend, frontend and mobile engineer agents.
A flag Claude Code sets when a stop hook already blocked this stop. Seeing it, the hook lets the stop through, so it can never loop.
The one line that ends a re-checked answer. The hook reads it as proof the pass already ran.
terms.example: Re-check: fixed the comma case in the parser

terms.means: The only copy of the prompt text, between two marker comments. The hook and the manual command both use it unchanged.
The session's log file, one JSON entry per message. The hook reads only its end.
Entries in the main transcript that belong to a subagent; the main session's turn leaves them out.
On any error, make no decision rather than block. A Stop hook that crashed into a block would stop every session from ending.

outline.title: main(payload): the re-check hook, as pseudocode

lines.code: if stop_hook_active: return {}             # never block one stop twice
mode, min_chars, subagents = config()      # env beats ~/.config/100x/recheck.json
if SubagentStop: skip if mode or subagents is off, or type not listed
if asked or the recheck skill ran: return {}
final = last_assistant_message or the turn's last text
if not (edited or len(final) >= min_chars): return {}
if a "Re-check:" line is in final: return {}
return block(reason = prompt file's marked block)

outline.title: scan(turn): did this turn edit anything?

lines.code: for each tool call Claude made in the turn:
if it is the recheck skill: already ran
edited |= tool in {Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit}
edited |= Bash matching sed -i, tee, git commit, > path
final = only the text after the last tool call

diagrams.title: When the hook holds a stop

diagrams.title: One held stop, call by call
diagrams.source:
sequenceDiagram
  %% level: 2
  actor Claude
  participant Host as Claude Code
  participant Hook as Re-check hook
  participant Gate as Stop gate
  participant Prompt as Prompt file
  Claude->>Host: end of turn
  Host->>Hook: Stop input
  Host->>Gate: Stop input
  Hook->>Prompt: read the marked block
  Hook-->>Host: block, reason is the prompt
  Host-->>Claude: re-check before stopping
  Claude->>Claude: three likely faults, checked against files
  Claude->>Host: end of turn again
  Host->>Hook: Stop input, already blocked
  Hook-->>Host: no decision
diagrams.caption: Both Stop hooks run side by side; when both block, their reasons arrive together, and on the next stop neither blocks again.

scenarios.title: An edit turn is held once for a second look

steps.t: You ask for a fix; Claude edits a file and answers in one line
Claude stops, and Claude Code runs both Stop hooks side by side
steps.d: The verification gate's Stop hook and this one run in parallel; if both block, both reasons arrive together.

steps.t: The hook checks this stop was not already blocked, and reads the mode
steps.d: The environment variable wins over the settings file; with neither, the mode is auto.
code: mode = env or recheck.json or auto

steps.t: It reads this turn from the end of the transcript
steps.d: Only the last {{tail_mib}} of the file is read. The turn is everything after your last real message; tool results and loaded skill text do not count as messages.

steps.t: The turn edited a file, so it counts as substantive
steps.d: An edit alone is enough, however short the answer; without one, the answer must reach {{min_chars}}.
do: edited: yes; answer length does not matter
code: if not (edited or len(final) >= min_chars): return {}

steps.t: No re-check has run yet: no command, no pasted prompt, no Re-check line
The hook blocks the stop, with the prompt file's text as the reason
steps.d: The prompt lives in one file between two markers, so the hook and the manual command can never drift apart.
do: block: assume this answer still has at least one mistake

steps.t: Claude names the likeliest faults and checks each against the files
steps.d: The prompt asks for {{faults}}, each settled from a file or a command run in this pass, never from memory.
do: read the callers, run the test
one input shape is parsed wrong

steps.t: Claude gives the corrected answer only, then one Re-check line
steps.d: No essay on what changed: graders marked that down, and the line is what tells the hook the pass already ran.
do: Fixed, both input shapes. Re-check: fixed the comma case

steps.t: Claude stops again, and this time the hook lets it through
steps.d: Claude Code marks this stop as already blocked, so the hook returns no decision.

scenarios.title: Which stops get a re-check, and which pass quietly

steps.t: A short answer with no edits passes quietly
steps.d: Below {{min_chars}} and nothing edited: short questions cost nothing.

steps.t: A shell command that writes a file counts as an edit
steps.d: In-place editors, tee, git commit, a Python file write, or output redirected to a path all count.

steps.t: A turn that already ran the re-check passes
steps.d: You typed the command, the prompt was pasted, the recheck skill was loaded, or the answer has a Re-check line.

steps.t: The last message comes straight from Claude Code, since the transcript can lag
steps.d: The file is written in the background and can miss the final message, so the length and Re-check line tests use the copy Claude Code passes in.
do: last message from the hook input wins over the transcript

steps.t: In manual or off mode, the main session is never held
Bad input or an internal error: the hook makes no decision
steps.d: It starts no subprocess, and any exception prints an empty answer, so a broken hook cannot stop a session from ending.

scenarios.title: Manual mode still re-checks the engineer subagents

steps.t: You switch re-check to manual
Your own turns now end without a re-check
A backend-engineer subagent finishes an edit, and its stop is held
steps.d: On a subagent stop only off, for the mode or the subagents setting, skips the check; manual is not tested there. The {{engineers}} engineer types are covered by default.
code: if mode == off or subagents == off: return {}

steps.t: A subagent type not on the list, such as code-reviewer, is let through
The code says this on purpose; the skill's mode table reads otherwise
steps.d: The hook's own description says manual and off never block a Stop and that off also disables subagents. The skill's table says manual runs only when you type the command. One of the two should change; until then, set subagents to off as well if you want no automatic passes at all.
do: for no automatic passes: mode manual and subagents off

scenarios.title: What if the hook blocked every stop?

steps.t: Claude stops again, and the hook blocks again
And again: each pass costs another minute or two
The turn can never end on its own

scenarios.title: Fix: block once per stop, and treat a Re-check line as done

steps.t: Claude stops again; Claude Code marks the stop as already blocked
steps.d: One pass is what was measured to help; a third was never measured.

steps.t: The hook lets it through; the Re-check line alone would have too
The verification gate's Stop hook follows the same once rule
steps.d: On the first stop both hooks may block together; on the next, neither does.

options.label: Hold each substantive turn once, automatically
pros: The pass that caught the bug happens without anyone remembering it
cons: Each held turn takes {{followup_min}} to {{followup_max}} longer
The same model checks itself, so it helps only when it opens the files

options.label: Only when you type the command
cons: The second look happens only if someone thinks to ask, which is when it is least needed

options.label: Every turn, however short
cons: Pays the cost on questions where nothing in code can be wrong

options.label: Repeat until an answer comes back unchanged
cons: A third pass was never measured
A Stop hook that loops stops the session from ending

decision.deciding_factor: On a silent money bug, {{first_safe}} were safe and {{second_safe}} were, while the wording barely mattered, so one routine pass on turns that change things is the cheapest win.
decision.revisit_when: A measured third pass beats the second, or the time a held turn costs pushes people to manual.

checks.q: Claude's final answer was a single line. Will the hook still hold this stop?
checks.answer: Yes. The turn edited a file, and an edit alone makes a turn substantive, whatever the answer's length.

checks.q: Claude stops again after the re-check. Does the hook block a second time?
checks.answer: No. Claude Code marks the stop as already blocked, and the answer also carries a Re-check line; either one lets it through.

checks.q: Re-check is set to manual. A backend-engineer subagent just finished an edit. Is its stop held?
checks.answer: Yes. Manual only spares the main session; only off, or subagents set to off, spares the engineers.

notes.config: Reads mode, min_chars and subagents from the settings file, then lets the two environment variables override them; anything unreadable falls back to the defaults.
notes.prompt_text: Returns the text between the prompt file's two markers, without its code fence, from the plugin root; None when the file or a marker is missing.
notes.blocks: The content blocks of a transcript entry; a plain string becomes one text block.
notes.is_file: True when the value is a path to an existing file.
notes.allowed: True when subagents is all, or the agent type matches a listed name exactly or without its plugin prefix.
notes.main: The hook: skips an already-blocked stop, applies the mode and the subagent list, reads the turn, and blocks once with the prompt when the turn is substantive and not yet re-checked.
